item.title: Mauricio Pochettino defends controversial Matthijs de Ligt call after Man Utd’s 4-0 Anfield humiliation by Liverpool
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-LIVERPOOL-MAN UTD - AFP Mauricio Pochettino has defended his eyebrow-raising decision to throw Matthijs de Ligt straight into Manchester United’s starting XI for his debut in charge during a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. The new Red Devils boss explained why he handed the Dutchman his first Premier League start in nearly a year. Pochettino stands by De Ligt selection The Dutch international had not featured in the league for 357 days due to a long-term back injury, yet found himself thrown into the heat of a North West derby . United’s defensive frailties were exposed almost immediately when De Ligt misjudged a long ball, allowing Alexander Isak to sprint through on goal. This error forced Leny Yoro into the desperate challenge that led to his dismissal. Goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz soon followed, before Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout in the second half. Despite the defender appearing slow and lethargic as he struggled with the pace of the game, Pochettino defended the selection following the final whistle. "He was training, he played in the Champions League before the international duty. I think when we arrived, we saw the combination [with Lisandro Martinez]," Pochettino told Sky Sports . Furious boss slams refereeing double standards The game-changing decision left Pochettino absolutely seething, with the manager quick to highlight a glaring double standard in the officiating following an earlier, unpunished penalty shout involving Jeremy Jacquet. Convinced that the referee's inconsistency completely altered the complexion of the match, Pochettino didn't hold back in his post-match assessment. "And I repeat again, Jacquet was a penalty, and if the referee says that is a penalty, for sure that action after never comes, and maybe we talk in another way," a frustrated Pochettino declared. "One centre-back made a mistake, was penalty, wasn't punished, and us, we made one mistake and we were punished. Now I accept all the situation, but the circumstances are the circumstances. It's so important to put the circumstance in front. Always." Reality check for new regime The defeat extends United’s winless streak in the Premier League to nine matches, marking the club's worst-ever run in the competition's history. Pochettino was seen in deep discussion with the officiating crew after the game, though he admitted that his protests would do little to change the outcome of his first match in charge. He emphasized the need for his squad to take responsibility for their performance while remaining critical of the external factors that influenced the game. "I have to defend my club," the Argentine coach stated. "And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card." item.title: KenPom has a bleak season ahead for Mark Pope and Kentucky Basketball
item.description: LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - NOVEMBER 13: Mark Pope the head coach oof the Kentucky Wildcats gives instructions to his team against the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks at Rupp Arena on November 13, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images KenPom projections aren’t the be-all, end-all of college basketball, and plenty of teams have made Ken Pomeroy’s algorithm look foolish by the time March rolls around. At the same time, his numbers aren’t something you can simply shrug off and pretend don’t exist either. When a model that tracks every single possession in Division I basketball starts flashing bright red warning lights, it is usually telling you something you already saw with your own eyes. Following Friday night’s 90-76 loss to Indiana in Indianapolis, KenPom released its latest update, and it is the last thing Big Blue Nation wanted to see. Breaking down Kentucky’s latest KenPom numbers Coming into the 2026-27 season, Kentucky sat just outside the KenPom preseason top 25 at No. 26. After early stumbles against Kansas and a narrow escape against Northern Arizona, the Wildcats had already tumbled outside the top 50. The 14-point defeat to the Hoosiers only accelerated the freefall. They are now No. 63 overall, No. 24 in adjusted offense and 131 in adjusted defense. The projected record is now sitting at 16-16 (6-12). That would be a disaster, much like Kentucky’s defense. The Cats can’t keep anyone out of the lane and are almost always in a rotation. And yet, the same defense keeps getting trotted out. Maybe try a zone? It surely couldn’t be much worse. The headline number that hurts the most As ugly as a 16-16 overall projection looks on paper, the real gut punch shows up when you scroll through the game-by-game forecast. Right now, KenPom projects Kentucky to be favored in just one SEC game : South Carolina. Kentucky is projected to be favored in just one SEC game, according to KenPom. pic.twitter.com/fMFy3SUIiN — Jeff Borzello (@jeffborzello) November 21, 2026 Out of an 18-game conference slate, the Wildcats are currently projected as the underdog in 17 of them. Reality vs. the numbers Now, let’s keep some perspective. too. Kentucky is going to win more than one SEC game, and they will probably win more than 8. Basketball isn’t played on a spreadsheet, and even KenPom’s own math agrees, which is why the overall forecast still pegs the Wildcats for a 6-12 conference finish rather than 1-17. Over the course of an 18-game grind, teams steal road games, catch fire at Rupp Arena, and pull off upsets. But the fact that Kentucky could enter almost every single conference game as the underdog is not something that should ever be uttered. Being a slight dog on the road against top-10 caliber SEC heavyweights like Florida, Alabama, or Texas is one thing. But Mississippi State, Vandy, and Ole Miss? Come on. This is Kentucky Basketball. item.title: Patriots expected to show interest in Daniel Jones, but there’s a catch
item.description: With their season at a crossroads in light of the fractured fibula suffered by starting quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots are exploring the possibility of adding another passer to the mix. One name to keep an eye on is Daniel Jones, who was let go by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday . Jones, 29, was placed on waivers, meaning that any team has the opportunity to claim him. However, according to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, that is not expected to happen. And once he makes it through the wire and to the open market, the Patriots are among the teams expected to take a look at him. “The Patriots along with the Baltimore Ravens and maybe the Arizona Cardinals are expected to have interest in the recently-waived former Colts starter,” Rapoport said on the air on Sunday. “He goes on waivers. We find out 4 p.m. on Monday whether or not anyone claims him. Unlikely because of the $2 million due this year, $10 million guaranteed for injury next year.” With Maye potentially missing the next six weeks , if not more, the Patriots are looking at a starter-backup combination of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Adding Jones to the mix would therefore make sense given his experience in the NFL and the fact that he has played some winning football previously in his career. However, there is a catch: the former first-round draft pick appears to be willing to wait for the right opportunity to come along. “If he clears [waivers], my understanding is that Daniel Jones is expected to wait,” Rapoport said. “Just to wait, see if there’s another quarterback injury. Of course, if there was, he would be the first call of any playoff team needing a quarterback.” If Jones is indeed in no rush to sign with a team, the Patriots’ interest might just start to evaporate. At 5-5 and the current eighth playoff seed in the AFC, they simply might not have time to wait for Jones. Instead, they might just try their luck with DeVito — who is in his second year in the system — rather than try to bring Jones aboard late and then try to get him up to starter-caliber speed. The Patriots, with DeVito currently atop their quarterback depth chart, will visit the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12.

item.title: OKC nail artist's TikTok went viral. Now she does Jared McCain's nails
item.description: When Jared McCain was traded to the Oklahoma City Thunder, Yvie McCrary saw more than basketball news. She saw a potential client. The Oklahoma City nail artist took her shot on TikTok, posting a video in hopes of catching McCain's attention. It went viral. He saw it. And soon, the NBA guard known for his elaborate manicures was sitting at McCrary's nail table. Months later, McCrary painted McCain's nails gold for Thunder media day . When he flashed them to The Oklahoman during a news conference, video of the manicure generated more than a million views on the NBA's social account. It was quite a leap for an artist barely three years into her career. And another sign of how nail art, long coded as feminine, is finding an increasingly visible place in men's fashion, including among professional athletes. McCain first found an interest in nail artistry during the COVID-19 pandemic, in his early years of high school. With nothing to do at home, he saw others do it online and decided to give it a try. "I liked the way it looked, and it became a unique part of something that I do, and now it's just part of me," McCain told The Oklahoman during OKC Thunder media day. Before he was playing professional basketball, he was already finding ways to bring nail art onto the court. During the basketball playoffs in high school, McCain painted his nails with the logo of each team his team defeated. By the time they won the championship, all five fingers represented stops along the title run. The hobby followed McCain to the NBA. He was drafted by the Philadelphia 76ers in the 2024 NBA Draft and later traded to Oklahoma City in February 2026. It has also become part of his brand. In a sports world filled with Nike, Adidas and Jordan partnerships, McCain has a deal with nail polish brand Sally Hansen. But when McCain arrived in Oklahoma City, he still needed someone to actually do his nails. That's where McCrary came in. OKC nail artist shoots her shot McCrary had just celebrated her two-year "nail birthday," as she calls it, when she learned McCain was headed to Oklahoma City. McCrary posted a TikTok for fun, with hopes of getting the shooting guard's attention, and after the video went viral, it landed on McCain’s feed. "He messaged me and wanted to come get nails; that was pretty cool for me," McCrary said. McCrary started cosmetology school in 2022, dreaming of becoming a hair stylist, but as part of the course, she needed to take a nail class. McCrary didn't think she was going to like it at first, but fell in love with the art once she got into it. "It's so versatile," McCrary said. "You can get pretty creative with it. ... A lot of people get single colors or clean girl nails and I'm like, 'Nope!' I like all the art; I like to do all the crazy fun things." item.title: Chelsea eye double winter swoop for Monaco's Lamine Camara and Bournemouth's Alex Scott despite Liverpool threat
item.description: Liverpool FC v AS Monaco - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Chelsea are considering a January double swoop for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and Bournemouth star Alex Scott as they look to reinforce their engine room. Despite facing serious competition from Premier League rivals Liverpool, officials in west London remain confident of convincing both players to join them in the New Year. Blues target two midfield additions TEAMtalk reports that Chelsea have not ruled out signing both Camara and Scott when the transfer window reopens. The Blues' lack of midfield depth was exposed at the weekend when Moises Caicedo suffered an early injury during their 4-1 defeat to Leeds United . Recruitment chiefs believe the pair offer different tactical qualities in central midfield, despite both operating in similar areas. Summer collapse fails to deter Chelsea originally targeted Camara late in the summer window as they scrambled to replace Enzo Fernandez following his move to Manchester City. A transfer had been lined up with Monaco before the Principality club pulled the plug at the last minute , sparking considerable annoyance inside Stamford Bridge. However, the report states that Chelsea have not held that collapsed deal against the Senegalese international himself. Club officials have remained in regular contact with his camp and closely tracked his progress throughout the current campaign, with Camara responding impressively by playing every single minute of Monaco's Ligue 1 season so far. Liverpool threat complicates winter pursuit Alongside their ongoing pursuit of Camara, Chelsea have also been making steady progress on a prospective deal for Scott. The outlet adds that Bournemouth are ready to do business on the midfielder after he rejected numerous offers to extend his current contract at the Vitality Stadium. Winning the race for either target will not be straightforward, as both players are widely expected to be on the move in January and are attracting major interest from across the top flight. Liverpool are known to be huge admirers of the midfield duo, with Anfield boss Andoni Iraola keen to boost his own options, setting up a potential New Year tug-of-war. item.title: Marc Marquez makes history, Valentino Rossi keeps revisiting it
item.description: Motorsport photo In one of those curious twists of fate, Marquez sealed his eighth MotoGP world title at Portimo just as Rossi was touring Italy to promote his autobiography, La Mia Storia , which was released on 10 November. Throughout those appearances, mainly on television and radio programmes, references to Marquez were a constant feature, subsequently picked up and amplified by the media. Not only by the specialist publications, but also by plenty of others with little connection to motorcycle racing, unwilling to pass up the opportunity to cash in on some particularly lucrative clicks. As for the substance of Rossi's message, there was nothing new: he was simply reiterating his long-held views on Marquez. The same views he has repeated for the past 11 years, ever since the 'Sepang Clash', the incident that forever divided the motorcycling world into Rossi and Marquez camps, and about which far too much has already been said and written. Ever since the Spaniard burst onto the MotoGP scene like a thunderbolt in 2013, he has been competing with the Italian for just about everything. On the track, for points, victories and titles. Off it, for the right to occupy the throne reserved for the rider regarded as the GOAT – the greatest of all time. That particular contest is impossible to settle if statistics – which now favour Marquez – are taken out of the equation, because any judgement is entirely subjective, shaped by personal opinions, admiration and allegiances towards either rider. With Rossi having retired five years ago and Marquez still winning, if there is one thing that continues to set them against each other, it is the narrative. Or, more precisely, the way that narrative is manipulated. As 'The Doctor' himself has acknowledged in recent days, he has still not recovered from the bitter disappointment of 2015. "It's something that doesn't go away; it still hurts. More than 10 years have passed, but the feeling and my state of mind when I think back to it are exactly the same as they were that night in Valencia, and that worries me a little," he admitted just a few days ago, during one of his many promotional appearances. It was a disappointment which, it is worth remembering, came after Rossi had pursued a disastrous strategy, seemingly devised by his worst enemy or, at the very least, by someone with a remarkable lack of judgement. The plan succeeded in reawakening a Marquez who had nothing left to play for in a championship that had already become an exclusively Yamaha affair. item.title: Ravens drop 6th straight to Panthers, put season on life support
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens dropped their sixth straight game in a rollicking, back-and-forth 35-33 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon. After a wild 58 minutes that included seven lead changes and no less than a dozen jaw-dropping plays, Carolina took the lead on a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal with 1:47 to go. Baltimore’s potential game-winning drive was snuffed out by a Jacoby Brissett interception, and the Ravens dropped to 4-7 . The currently sit 11th in the AFC – and in the 2027 draft order. That is starting to sound like a good thing for a team that should be considering major changes this offseason. The Ravens defense gave up the lead four different times on Sunday afternoon, including twice directly after scores from the offense. The offense turned the ball over twice and gained just eight yards across their first three drives of the second half. And outside of a Devontez Walker kickoff return touchdown, Baltimore’s special teams units struggled with sloppy ball-handling and poor coverage. And yet, the Ravens had two distinct chances to win this game late in the fourth quarter. The first was the Panthers’ penultimate drive, in which Baltimore’s defense could not dig their heels in and protect a one-point lead. Brissett’s gunslinging on the previous drive showed he was capable of driving into field goal range, but another collapse in pass protection forced him to throw a prayer out of bounds to avoid a sack. Except the pass did not make it to the sidelines, instead landing in the arms of Panthers linebacker Tyrel Dodson. In both instances, the Ravens could not be at their best when their best was needed. Despite thrilling wins over the Cowboys and Falcons, first-year head coach Jesse Minter’s oft-repeated mantra never fully took root in The Castle. And it is fair to question if he has lived up to his own standard. Brissett was rushing partially because Minter declined to take a timeout after a sack with 1:30 to go. 24 seconds later, Brissett threw a checkdown to Justice Hill to set up a 4th-and-1. Only then did Minter stop the clock, only for Brissett to restart it with a sneak that chewed up another 23 seconds before the pick. This is the second game in a row that Minter’s questionable timeout usage has costed the Ravens precious time in end-of-half situations – two contests that were decided by a total of five points. At the end of the day, the coaching staff is failing simple math problems – and struggling to keep their finger on the pulse of the game. To be fair, that pulse was all over the play. To borrow a phrase from a Saturday Night Live great, this game had everything: a replay-assisted safety; a wildcat flea flicker touchdown; a fumble out of the end zone, a muffed punt, and Walker’s return touchdown – all from the Ravens, all in the first 20 minutes. item.title: Giants QB Jameis Winston restrains teammate Malik Nabers during angry moment on the touchline
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images New York Giants QB Jameis Winston’s veteran instincts kicked in during a heated moment involving 23-year-old WR Malik Nabers during their 23-18 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Giants are proving to be more competitive than many had assumed before the season, with their 6-3-1 record putting them in pole position to secure the NFC East and a spot in the playoffs one season after going 4-13. One of the key reasons for this turnaround has been WR Nabers, who tore his ACL last season. While Nabers is impressing fans on the field with his raw prowess and route-running skills, he also needs to ensure he stays level-headed and focused on winning. Malik Nabers needed to be calmed down by Jameis Winston during Giants win With under six minutes left in this closely poised contest, Nabers was visibly upset on the touchline when the Giants’ defence was on the field, with backup QB Winston restraining the young WR. This situation has since been downplayed, as neither Nabers nor Winston had anything negative to say about the seemingly tense confrontation. Nabers claims to have just been saying he was good while passionately cheering the defence on from the touchline. It seems to be a moment of excessive passion flowing out in the middle of a close game between two teams that hope to make runs in the playoffs. Nabers went 7/12 on receptions for 55 yards and one touchdown in this game. He has gone 65/97 all season for 747 receiving yards and three TDs. He is looking like he’s back to peak fitness and willing to do anything to help the Giants add to their win column. Winston was the Giants’ starting QB earlier this season after Jaxson Dart was ruled out for the season after Week 2. He has since transitioned into a backup/mentor role after the team acquired former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings. The passion on display from Nabers and the leadership from Winston both are great signs for a once-proud franchise hoping to become a competitive force again. item.title: Atletico's Simeone breaks La Liga victories record
item.description: Diego Simeone beat the record of Luis Aragones, who recorded his final La Liga victory in 2004 [Getty Images] Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club. Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight. Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total. "It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games. "I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this." Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face". He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it. "This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?" The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain. He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure. Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later. He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign. Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge. However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016. Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018. His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse

NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
